stories.author: shdon
stories.title: Quake Shareware, a CD-ROM just a little too full
stories.groq_label: id Software's Quake shareware CD-ROM included encrypted full versions of their past games to cut out retailers, but gamers cracked it in 39 days, leaving 150,000 unsold discs.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Community Perspective:

The Hacker News community generally responded to this article about Quake Shareware with positive reactions. Many commenters appreciated the nostalgic value of the shareware disc and considered it a memorable part of their gaming history. Others highlighted the soundtrack as a standout feature, noting its uniqueness and quality. Nevertheless, recurring criticisms focused on the shareware model's limitations, particularly the ease of cracking and the inability to unlock certain content (e.g., Final Doom) using tools like QCRACK. As a whole, commenters viewed the project as an interesting piece of gaming history while acknowledging its flaws and the ingenuity of its distribution strategy.
stories.groq_explain: The idea was to sell *Quake* on a CD-ROM with extra space, including encrypted copies of all past id Software games. Buyers could call a number to unlock the full game after purchase. But hackers cracked it in weeks, letting people unlock everything for free. The plan backfired, leaving id Software with 150,000 unsellable CDs. It shows how early digital distribution ideas struggled against piracy and logistics.
